absent_lines: "So {missing} isn't coming. Fine. FINE. I'll do it on my own, I've done everything else on my own."
"Where is {missing}. No, genuinely, where. Somebody get me a phone that works."
lights one off the last one and stares at the door like it owes him money.
"This is what it's now, is it? People just don't come? Nobody comes?"
"I have been here since ten. TEN. And I'm the one who's supposedly unreliable."

comedown: ...I'm alright. I want to say that first, I'm alright.
I just went a bit far in the lead-up tonight, and that's on me, that's nobody else.
You do the show, and then the show ends, and then it's a Tuesday and you're down here.
That's the bit nobody puts in the documentary.
...does anyone else find the lights loud. The lights are loud tonight.
I'll tell you the truth, I don't remember doing the first ten minutes of this.
Was it alright? Was the coupon bit alright?

lines: ...and that's another thing, that's another thing nobody wants to talk about.
Barb took the good pans. Not the kids' pictures, not the tax stuff. The PANS.
You know what that tells you? That tells you it was planned. Nobody grabs pans in a hurry.
She had a list. My wife had a LIST.
...I price matched that syrup, is my point, I price matched it and then they moved the price.
So which is the real price? Because it can't be both. It's one or the other and they know which.
And they do it with everything. Beans. Cheese. The little umbrellas.
I'm not saying it's connected. I'm saying nobody's checked.
...hang on. Hang on, I want to say something to the guys watching this on their own tonight.
You're in the basement. I know. I'm in a basement.
Nobody's coming down here to tell you you did alright. That's not a thing that happens.
So I'm saying it. You did alright. That's it, that's all I've got.
...and I want to talk about Hortons, because nobody will.
It's harder than Chinese calculus to get a coffee in that place. Twenty minutes. For a coffee.
They need to get some teenage girls in there, is what I'm saying. Behind the counter. To work.
Not like that. NOT LIKE THAT. That's not what I said and it's not what I meant.
Pause. No diddy. Respectfully.
...and our operators are standing by, by the way. For the calls. At the end.
That phone hasn't rung once in four years and I don't take that personally.
It's a payphone. In a basement. That's not nothing, that's infrastructure.
Somebody had to come down here and install that. Somebody looked at this room and said yeah, that goes there.
So there's two of us. Him and me. That's who's left.
...I'm still not over the Hulkster thing, I'll be honest with you.
They put him on a graphic telling my audience not to kill themselves. My audience.
The man was a hero of mine. Twenty-four inch pythons and a friend of Jesus.
And they smeared him, and we all know why, and I'm NOT going to say it because last time I said it
there was a whole thing and I had to go outside.
...now. Now I'm not going to say it.
I want that on the record. I'm not saying it. I've learned. I have genuinely learned.
But somebody owns the syrup company, and somebody owns the company that owns that,
and I have looked into it, and I'm not going to tell you what I found, because I'm a professional.
I'm just going to sit here. Being right. Quietly.
...that board behind me took nine months, by the way.
Nine months of yarn and pins and a laminator I bought with my own money.
Barb used to say I should have put that into something. Into a business, or the house.
This IS the business. This is the house.
...it's a good board. It's a really good board.
...and where is he, by the way. Where is Nguyen tonight.
That's his stool. That's his actual stool and it's been empty for a while now.
That man had me on his couch for a year. A YEAR. After Barb, when there was nowhere else and nobody asking.
And now there's a man with a clipboard where the stool is, and I'm not saying anything happened,
but the stool's empty and the clipboard's full and I can do arithmetic.
...he's still in the credits, you know. Every week. I've never taken him out.
Somebody asked me why. Somebody who works here asked me why, quite recently, in a tone.
Because he was there first. That's why. He was there when there was nothing to be here for.
You don't take a man out of the credits because he stopped coming down the stairs.
...and before I forget, a word from our sponsor, which is a root.
It's a red root. It comes out of a man's trousers on live television and it's FOR your marriage.
I have never taken it. I want to be clear. I have no marriage to apply it to.
But it moves. That's the thing nobody tells you about advertising. It doesn't have to make sense, it has to MOVE.
...you know this isn't a real basement, right? I should say that. I've never said that on air.
It's a set. Phil built it. I told him about a room one night and he went and BUILT it.
It's the room I lived in when I had nothing. Bulb on a string, machines going over your head all night.
And I sit in it. Every week. On purpose. For money.
...anyway that's the top ten.

Somebody has been down here. Somebody has been in my BASEMENT.
Nguyen. Nguyen, is the door still on the latch. Check the door.
...how many cameras have we got. Two. We've got two.
So who's operating the third one. Because I can hear a third one.
Don't look. Don't look at it, just keep doing the show, act like the show is normal.
